ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The top of the figure is the +VCC power supply node; the upper-right resistor R is connected from +VCC to the detection/emitter node on one side of the transistor. This node is fed back to one input terminal of the operational amplifier, and on the left side, the reference branch labeled Vref and R1 form the reference input. The op-amp output drives the transistor base through R2; below the transistor is connected the load resistor RL, and the load current IO passes through RL. Reasoning: According to ideal negative feedback, the op-amp adjusts the transistor base so that the voltage across resistor R is stabilized at Vref. Therefore, the transistor emitter current set by R is IE = Vref/R. The current in load RL is the transistor collector current IC. For a transistor with current gain beta, IE = IC + IB and IC = beta IB, so IC = beta/(beta+1) * IE. Therefore IO = IC = (beta/(beta+1)) * Vref/R.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit: R connects from +VCC to the transistor-side sense node, the op-amp compares that node with Vref, and RL carries the transistor output current. With ideal feedback, the voltage across R is regulated to Vref, so the transistor emitter current set by R is IE = Vref/R. Since the load current through RL is the collector current, convert emitter current to collector current using IC = (beta/(beta+1)) IE. Thus IO = (beta/(beta+1)) Vref/R.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit connections: the reference Vref is applied to the op-amp positive input, the negative input senses the node associated with R and the transistor, and RL is fed by the transistor current. Ideal feedback makes the sensed node match Vref, so the current supplied through R is IR = Vref/R. At the transistor, this current is the emitter current and splits into load/collector current IO plus base current IB. Since beta = IO/IB, IB = IO/beta. Write Vref/R = IO + IO/beta, then solve for IO to get IO = (beta/(beta+1)) Vref/R.
